timeline: 1990: First appears in print in Hungary.
1990s: Gains popularity as a faster alternative to Preferansz.
Present: Played in Hungarian card circles alongside Ulti.
history.cultural: Reflects the strong Central European tradition of 3-player cutthroat card games.
history.evolution: The game simplifies the bidding and contract structure of Tarokk while retaining the 'Talon' exchange and the 'Last Tricks' bonus mechanic.

setup.players: Three players. No partnerships; the highest bidder becomes the declarer and plays alone against the other two defenders. Deal and play are clockwise.
setup.deck: 36-card French-suited deck (remove 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s). Rank: A (high) > K > Q > J > 10 > 9 > 8 > 7 > 6.
setup.dealing: Deal 11 cards to each player. The remaining 3 cards form the face-down 'Talon'.
setup.equipment: Standard deck stripped to 36 cards, score sheet.

rules.objective: For the soloist: Win at least 6 tricks. For the defenders: Prevent the soloist from winning 6 tricks.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Bidding**: Players bid the number of talon cards they wish to exchange. Hierarchy (lowest to highest): 'Three', 'Two', 'One', 'Hand' (Solo/Zero). 2. **The Exchange**: The winner takes the specified number of cards from the talon, adds them to their hand, and discards the same number. (In 'Hand' bids, the talon is ignored). 3. **Trump Selection**: The soloist declares a Trump suit. 4. **Announcements**: Before play, the soloist may announce 'ArrivÃ¡zs' (winning the last 3 tricks). Defenders can 'Double' (Kontra) the game or the announcement. 5. **Play**: Soloist leads first. Standard trick rules (follow suit). 6. **Scoring**: Winning 6+ tricks wins the game. Winning < 6 loses. ArrivÃ¡zs is scored separately.
keyRules: Bidding Hierarchy: Taking FEWER cards is a HIGHER bid. (Hand > One > Two > Three).
ArrivÃ¡zs: A commitment to win tricks 9, 10, and 11. Can be announced or performed silently (for half score).
Kontra (Double): Defenders can double the game score or the ArrivÃ¡zs score independently.
Talon constraints: If you bid 'Two', you look at top 2 talon cards only. 'One' looks at top 1.

strategy.basic: Bid conservatively. Only bid 'Hand' or 'One' if you have a very strong suit and Side Aces.
strategy.intermediate: The Discard: When exchanging with the talon, try to create a 'Short Suit' (void) to ruff (trump) early tricks. Keep Kings and Queens if you have the Ace, or discard them if they are unguarded.
strategy.advanced: ArrivÃ¡zs Setup: Save your highest trumps for the end. You need complete control of tricks 9, 10, and 11 to win the bonus.
tips: Always check the 'Kontra' risk. If your hand is borderline, don't announce ArrivÃ¡zs.
Defenders should lead trumps if they think the soloist is relying on ruffing a void suit.

variations.name: Open Talon
variations.description: Discarded talon cards are shown to defenders.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Open Talon only changes information visibility for the talon; base engine rules remain the same.

scoring.description: Base points are multiplied by the bid level and any Doubles.
scoring.winCondition: Highest score after a set number of rounds or reaching a target (e.g., 50).

synthesis.shortDescription: Three-player trick game from Hungary. Bid how many talon cards to exchange, declare trump, and try for Arrivázs (last three tricks).
